questions.question: What is the difference between ${...} and #{...} inside @Value?
options: ${...} reads a configuration key, #{...} evaluates a Spring expression
${...} evaluates an expression, #{...} reads a configuration key
They are two spellings of the same thing
${...} is only for numbers, #{...} is only for text
questions.explanation: A dollar placeholder looks up a property key, while a hash expression is calculated by the Spring Expression Language.

questions.question: How do you make a @Value setting optional with a fallback?
questions.explanation: The text after the first colon inside the placeholder is the default that is used when the key is missing.

questions.question: application.properties has fee=30. A bean has @Value("#{${fee} * 2}") int express. What does express hold?
questions.explanation: Spring first replaces ${fee} with 30, then the expression 30 * 2 is calculated, giving 60.

questions.question: The file has branches=Pune,Nashik,Nagpur and a bean has @Value("${branches}") List<String> b. What is b.size()?
questions.explanation: Spring converts a comma separated line into a list with one item per comma separated value, so the size is 3.

questions.question: A bean uses @Value("${clinic.name}") but the key is missing from every configuration source. What happens?
options: The field stays null and the app starts
The field becomes an empty string
The app fails at startup with 'Could not resolve placeholder'
Spring reads the value from the database
questions.explanation: Without a default, an unresolved placeholder stops the bean from being created, so startup fails early.
